sentences.text: 1. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Ajay Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Praveen Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and Sri Brijesh Kumar Dwivedi, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the orders dated 08.05.2024, 05.06.2024, 01.07.2024, 22.07.2024, 26.08.2024 issuing the bailable warrants and thereafter Non-bailable warrants in Complaint Case No.244896 of 2022 (Tulika Sharma Vs Sunny Seth and Another), under Sections- 498-A, 323, 504,
506 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station-Kalyanpur, District- Kanpur Nagar.
4.

entities.text: Tulika Sharma Vs Sunny Seth and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned counsel for opposite party no.2 have jointly submitted that parties have settled their dispute amicably and an application u/s 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 has also been filed before the Family Court, Kanpur Nagar.

Copy of the same has been annexed at page no.9 of the supplementary affidavit and request is made that on the basis of compromise,
impugned proceeding may be quashed.
5. However, learned AGA has pointed out that there is no verified compromise on record, therefore, parties may be directed to file compromise before the court below and get it verified.

6. Considering the aforesaid submission, present application is disposed of with a direction to the applicants that they will file original deed of compromise before the court below within a period of 15 days.

In case, such compromise is filed then court below will verify the same after summoning the parties, within a period of next one month and after verification of the compromise, court below may terminate the proceeding on the basis of aforesaid compromise.
7. It is further provided that applicants are at liberty to file fresh 482 application to quash the impugned proceeding on the basis of verified compromise, if need arises."
6. Thereafter, the compromise stood verified by the court below, ACJM, Kanpur Nagar on 07.03.2025 (Annexure-4, starting from page-29 onwards, relevant extract at page-34 of the paper-book).

However, the court below by virtue of its order dated 08.05.2025 came to the concluded that the offences are not compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC, though the Sunny Seth And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 30 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161012854/
2 verification was done.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that once the parties themselves have entered into compromise, thus this Court may exercise the inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC/ 528 of BNSS and quash the proceedings.

7. Learned A.G.A. as well as counsel for O.P. No. 2 have no objection to the same and according to them, the compromise stood entered and the certified copy thereof is already on record.
8.

Considering the submissions so made across the Bar bearing in mind the factum that the compromise stands verified and respectfully following the judgment in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, 2012(10) SCC 303, State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan, 2019 (5) SCC 688 and B.S.
Joshi and others v. State of Haryana and another 2003 (4) SCC 675, the application stands allowed in the following manner:
